newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran marks Islamic revolution anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Iran marks Islamic revolution anniversary.

text.p: Crowds celebrating the 18th anniversary of Iran's Islamic revolution rallied in Tehran on Monday, cheering and brandishing posters of the late leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.
More than 100,000 men and women in black veils marched to a rally in Tehran, chanting the trademark slogans of the 1979 revolution: "Death to America" and "Death to Israel".
The official news agency IRNA said millions attended the rallies across Iran.
Addressing the Tehran rally, President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said Iranians backed the Islamic state because it was fulfilling the revolution's promise of freedom, independence and development.

"No one can deny that in today's Iran all national decisions regarding political, economic, cultural, scientific and defence issues are taken by Iranians and by representatives of the people," Rafsanjani said.
This contrasted with life under the late Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi's rule when the U.S. and British embassies "dictated the country's basic policies", he added.
A resolution read at the rally warned the United States and its Gulf Arab allies against any assaults on Iran.
"This nation of martyrdom and Jihad (holy war) would aim all its wrath against the glass palaces of reactionary puppets and the Great Satan's (U.S.) material interests," it said.

The warning came a day after Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who is also Iran's commander-in-chief, said regional states with close ties to foreign powers would be the first to suffer if the Gulf became instable.

Iran has rejected media reports that it was linked to the bombing of a U.S. military complex in Saudi Arabia last June that killed 19 American airmen. Some Tehran officials have said the reports indicated that Washington was preparing to attack Iran.
